concepts.why: The patient presented with a two-week history of an asymptomatic swelling in the right lower half of the face, and a clinical diagnosis of a nonspecific chronic abscess with buccal-space involvement was made.
The patient is a known diabetic on regular medication, and the gross right facial asymmetry could be related to diabetic cheilitis.
The contrast-enhanced CT of the face showed a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas in the right buccal space, which could be a buccal space cyst.
The patient presented with a 6 × 6 cm ovoid subcutaneous swelling with ill-defined borders and a consistency ranging from soft to firm, which could be related to necrotizing sialometaplasia.
The patient presented with reduced mouth opening and no lymphadenopathy, paresthesia, or facial palsy, which could be related to sialadenitis.
The patient presented with a two-week history of an asymptomatic swelling in the right lower half of the face, which could be a buccal mucosal abscess.
The patient has a history of two prior similar episodes over eight years, and is a known diabetic on regular medication, which could be related to a granulomatous disease.
The contrast-enhanced CT of the face showed a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas in the right buccal space, which could be a benign salivary gland tumor.

rationales.F01: Asymptomatic swelling in the right lower half of the face is consistent with a chronic buccal space abscess.
rationales.F02: Reduced mouth opening is a common symptom of buccal space abscess.
rationales.F06: Gross right facial asymmetry is a sign of a space-occupying lesion in the buccal space.
rationales.F07: A 6 × 6 cm ovoid subcutaneous swelling is consistent with a large abscess or cyst in the buccal space.
rationales.F10: Contrast-enhanced CT showing a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas in the right buccal space is highly suggestive of a chronic buccal space abscess.
rationales.F11: Intracystic loculations with dense cystic content and erosion of the posterior buccal cortex are characteristic of a chronic buccal space abscess.
rationales.F12: A clinical diagnosis of a nonspecific chronic abscess with buccal-space involvement is highly suggestive of a chronic buccal space abscess.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's history of recurrent asymptomatic swellings, reduced mouth opening, and imaging findings of a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas in the right buccal space support the diagnosis of a chronic buccal space abscess.
